newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends up despite poor results.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends up despite poor results.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended marginally higher on Wednesday, despite poor sentiment caused by the announcement of bad 1996 results by several firms, analysts said.
The index rose 0.38 points or 0.21 percent to end at 176.27 on turnover of HK$149.9 million against Tuesday's HK$148.3 million.
Investors sold firms which posted weak 1996 results, capping further gains by the B share index, analysts said.
"The glaringly bad company results did not shock investors because they had expected poor earnings from those companies," an analyst at J&A Securities said.

Shenzhen Tellus Holdings Co Ltd, Hainan Pearl River Enterprises Holdings Ltd and Gintian Industry (Group) Co Ltd 0 003.SZ all announced losses for 1996 on Wednesday, the final day of the corporate results reporting season.
A handful of other B share companies also announced weaker 1996 earnings compared with 1995.
Conglomerate Tellus ended 3.90 percent higher at HK$3.20 after plunging to its 10 percent limit-down at HK$2.77 within the first few minutes of afternoon trading.
The company on Wednesday announced the sale of its state shares, amounting to 72.4 percent of its equity, to a state-owned company in Shenzhen.
"Investors are expecting improvements in the company's operations this year following the change in shareholding," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"But it also looks like some big players are manipulating share prices," the J&A analyst said.
Conglomerate Gintian was the biggest loser, falling HK$0.25 or 6.56 percent to HK$3.56.
"This stock is unlikely to fall much further as investors have digested the news of the company's poor annual results," the Guotai analyst said.
The index moved in a relatively narrow range ahead of a holiday on Thursday and Friday, analysts said.
The Shenzhen and Shanghai stock exchanges will be closed for the official Labour Day holiday and will open again on Monday.
The A share index gained 4.50 points or 0.93 percent to end at 489.22 on turnover of 11.7 billion yuan against Tuesday's 14.9 billion.
